note: tiffcp() (tools/tiffcp.c) reads the input TIFF's BitsPerSample directory tag into a local `bitspersample` via CopyField(TIFFTAG_BITSPERSAMPLE, bitspersample) -- fully attacker-controlled, since BitsPerSample is a plain directory field of the crafted input file. That value is passed to pickCopyFunc(), which uses it only to reject one unrelated combination (differing planar config w/ bitspersample!=8 && samplesperpixel>1) and otherwise selects cpContig2SeparateByRow/cpSeparate2ContigByRow purely from the in/out planar-config and tiled-ness -- never gating on bitspersample itself. Neither of those two selected copy functions re-reads or checks BitsPerSample (unlike their tiled siblings, e.g. cpSeparateTiles2ContigTiles, which do call TIFFGetField(..., TIFFTAG_BITSPERSAMPLE, ...) before copying). Both allocate inbuf/outbuf sized by TIFFScanlineSize() (which correctly accounts for the real, possibly-<8 BitsPerSample), but their row-copy loop unconditionally treats each sample as exactly 1 byte (`*outp++ = *inp; inp += spp;` for `n = imagewidth` iterations) -- so an image with BitsPerSample != 8 (e.g. `-p separate` on a 1-bit image) walks inp/outp far past the smaller buffers TIFFScanlineSize() actually sized: an OOB heap read (inp) and write (outp). Verified with a real CodeQL C/C++ database built from the buggy source: the query fires at exactly tools/tiffcp.c:1090 (cpContig2SeparateByRow) and tools/tiffcp.c:1143 (cpSeparate2ContigByRow, the same defect shape's second call site).
